reproduced.source: artifacts/reproduction/*/tfidf/name_context/metrics.json, computed directly from raw predictions.jsonl by scripts/reproduce_memory.py, run on evaluation/data/omap_mimic/omop_mimic_data.xlsx

dataset_actually_found.note: See dataset_report.json. num_rows and num_target_attributes match the brief; num_source_attributes matches one of the two on-disk copies of the file (240) but not the other (241); num_positive_pairs (129) does NOT match the brief's 197 -- not adjusted, reported as found.

difference.num_positive_pairs: brief says 197, dataset file has 129 -- a 68-pair (35%) discrepancy, unexplained; possibly a different dataset version was used for the thesis, or the brief's number includes pairs from a different/extended annotation pass not present in this repository copy.

encoder_blocked.sbert: sentence-transformers installed, but no network access to huggingface.co to download sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
encoder_blocked.biobert: sentence-transformers installed, but no network access to huggingface.co to download dmis-lab/biobert-base-cased-v1.2
encoder_blocked.clinicalbert: sentence-transformers installed, but no network access to huggingface.co to download emilyalsentzer/Bio_ClinicalBERT

conclusion: Only TF-IDF retrieval quality was reproduced in this sandbox, on the pair-level and source-attribute-level splits of the real OMOP-MIMIC dataset found in the repository. The thesis's ClinicalBERT/BioBERT claims could NOT be reproduced or refuted here due to lack of network access to download pretrained weights -- this is an environment limitation, not a code limitation (the Encoder adapters and full retrieval/metrics pipeline are implemented and tested; only weight download is blocked). The positive-pair count discrepancy (129 found vs 197 claimed) should be investigated against the exact dataset version used for the thesis before drawing further conclusions.
